title: parsing parimatch websocket data for local ml models, hitting latency overhead
author: Zealou-sidealIron
selftext: running a custom python script to scrape live sports lines to feed into a local ml model to calculate implied probability deltas. routing it through parimatch right now since their odds update fast enough to actually backtest the algorithm against real time line movement. the problem is their websocket dumps a massive nested json payload every second and the parsing overhead is bottlenecking the model's execution time. anyone here pulling live odds for ai predictive testing? are you guys building custom filters to strip the raw payload before feeding it to the model, or is there a cleaner hidden api endpoint to hit without getting rate limited?

comments.author: Upset_Dean13
comments.body: Yeah, you definitely need to build a custom filter before feeding it to the model. Dumping that raw nested JSON straight into your execution pipeline is always going to bottleneck it. Just strip the payload down to the specific match IDs and odds you actually need first. ​

comments.author: LawfulnessNew7429
comments.body: Don't bother looking for a hidden API endpoint, you'll just end up getting rate limited. Sticking with the websocket is the right play. Try using orjson in Python instead of the standard library, it handles those massive nested dumps way faster and should fix your latency. ​

replies.author: Zealou-sidealIron
replies.body: thanks for the tip, will definitely swap to orjson tonight. honestly even with the massive data dumps, im just really impressed parimatch doesn't instantly block or rate limit my account for keeping the socket open this long. their live client speed is seriously unmatched for this kind of stuff.
